reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes joining a sponsor-controlled left/right network, buying tokens, and an automated process presented as money mining that requires no further action. The speaker directly explains how to recruit and position members while encouraging participation in the token platform, rather than warning about or investigating the offer.

citations.quote: We want to promote the business
we've selected from the beginning the money mining to be automated
Later on, there is no need to do anything at all, because we've selected from the beginning the money mining to be automated
we always have a team to the left and one to the right
the minimum number being 50

opening.argument: The tutorial does not promise a profit or state that returns are guaranteed. It describes a token-order workflow and says the purchase process is automated, but that alone does not establish what the process earns or that a buyer will profit. The speaker also describes support and guidance from a sponsoring line, which is consistent with explaining how the platform's membership and account settings work, not certifying an investment outcome.

citations.quote: The bid option is where you can buy and sell tokens.
when it's time to buy the tokens rows, the mining process to automatic
providing support and guidance to you

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats the phrase “money mining” as a promise of effortless earnings, but the cited wording describes automation and does not state an amount, a return, or a guarantee. Nor does explaining member placement establish that viewers are being promised income from recruits. The evidence supports a tutorial about operating an account; it does not establish the financial outcome the prosecution attributes to it.

citations.quote: the company will automatically take it and place it in the mining process
how to position members in the network

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The speaker does more than describe a neutral interface: she says tokens are bought and then automatically placed into a process she calls “money mining,” with no further action required. Combined with instructions for promoting the business and positioning new members, this is a pitch for participation, even without a numerical return promise.

citations.quote: Later on, there is no need to do anything at all, because we've selected from the beginning the money mining to be automated
We want to promote the business

opening.argument: This is presented as an operational tutorial: the speaker says she wants to explain member positioning, demonstrates account settings, and walks through the token-buying interface. She explains where to enter an order and how to select a placement option. Showing a process is not, by itself, proof that its underlying service is legitimate or that its claims are true; the material here establishes instruction, not an independently verified investment result.

citations.quote: in this short video I want to explain how to position members in the network
I click on Save Settings
The bid option is where you can buy and sell tokens.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution reads promotional language into the tutorial, but the quoted “promote” passage explains what the interface link is for; it does not show a claim about guaranteed earnings. The network-placement instructions and order walkthrough are concrete operational content. Describing an automated setting does not establish how the mining process works or what result it produces, so the opening goes beyond what the demonstration itself proves.

citations.quote: We want to promote the business
click on the Place Order button and that's it.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial's subject is participation in the business, not an unrelated software operation: it instructs viewers how to recruit through a sponsor link, place members into left/right teams, buy tokens, and have them put into mining automatically. That combination makes the demonstration promotional, and its procedural tone does not neutralize the substance of the money-mining pitch.

opening.argument: The material shows a token marketplace with buy and sell options, an order form, and a displayed price chart. The speaker describes placing an order and navigating account menus, which can be read as ordinary platform use. The cited material does not state a guaranteed return, specify a payout, or explain a mechanism by which recruited members generate income for the viewer. A buy/sell tutorial and a reference to mining do not alone establish those missing terms.

citations.quote: The bid option is where you can buy and sell tokens.
the number of tokens we want to buy
the more you participate in your team, the more you will get support and guidance

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening points to a minimum order and member placement, but neither demonstrates a promised return or a downline payout. A displayed order interface establishes that tokens can be bought and sold; it does not establish the economics or outcome of that activity. The phrase “money mining” is not accompanied in the cited evidence by a specified yield or guarantee, so the accusation relies on implications rather than stated terms.

citations.quote: The bid option is where you can buy and sell tokens.
the minimum number being 50

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The ordinary-market framing omits the explicit link the speaker makes between token purchases and automated “money mining,” including that the company will take the purchased tokens and place them into that process. The video also teaches sponsor-led recruitment and team placement. Those are not merely neutral observations of a chart; they present a participation path tied to a mining-return proposition, even if no exact yield is stated.
